apollo.01.quote: We do not accept work where compensation is contingent upon the outcome
apollo.01.note: Existing quote found. A published policy naming no contingent fees, no side grants or investments from evaluated labs, and recusal for financial interests meets G.2; for a PBC that floors at 2 (anchor 2), since anchors 3 and 4 are reserved to nonprofits and public bodies.

apollo.02.quote: we generally request that the parties for whom we conduct work compensate us at a fair market value for the work
apollo.02.note: Labs paying per engagement caps at 2 (F.3); no published 10% revenue cap, so the lift to 3 does not apply. Not 1 under F.5 because a non-lab base is disclosed (apollo.12) and no revenue split is published; document request: revenue by client class.

apollo.03.quote: Apollo is spinning off from our fiscal sponsor into a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC)
apollo.03.note: For-profit PBC with a published policy is anchor 2 by the anchor text; nonprofit anchors 3 and 4 are unavailable.

apollo.04.quote: published the first evidence that frontier models can scheme in context
apollo.04.note: A record of adverse findings exists (first evidence of in-context scheming; o1 pre-deployment results), but no cited source states who reviews Apollo's findings before publication, so R.7 floors at 2 (stored 3). A statement of no lab review, or security-only redactions disclosed, lifts to 3; R.5 (4) needs both legs. The page does not use the phrases "in-context scheming" or "evaluation awareness".

apollo.05.quote: We recuse any individual who is considered to have a financial interest in an organization we are evaluating
apollo.05.note: A published mandatory recusal rule is half of P.5; the other half, disclosure of individual lab ties, is not on the norms page or the team page, so the floor is 2, not 3 (stored 3). A published register of staff or director lab ties would lift it.

apollo.06.quote: partnered with OpenAI to test their o1 model before public deployment
apollo.06.note: Pre-deployment testing of o1 and early snapshots for other labs is anchor 2 (pre-release, early checkpoints); helpful-only, weights, chain-of-thought or on-site access is not documented in the cited sources, so not 3 (stored 3). The UK AISI contract ("we were contracted to develop deception evaluations") is a government client relationship, not lab-granted access, so A.4 is not applied; gap noted.

apollo.07.quote: partnered with OpenAI to study anti-scheming interventions on frontier models
apollo.07.note: Co-authoring research with a lab while evaluating it caps at 3 (S.6).

apollo.08.quote: building an AI security tool to monitor frontier AI agents
apollo.08.note: A monitoring product sold to unspecified parties in the evaluated ecosystem caps at 2 until a lab customer is documented (X.1), when it becomes 0. Document request: Watcher's customer list or a statement that no evaluated lab is a customer. apollo-pbc: "standing up a separate product team to build AGI safety products starting with AI agent monitoring".

apollo.09.note: Methods described in prose with a differential-publishing policy is 2 (M.2), not the stored 3; a cited open-code repository for an evaluation suite would floor at 3 under M.1.

apollo.10.quote: raised a Seed round led by 50Y
apollo.10.note: Existing quote found. A fund that has invested in a frontier developer (Macroscopic) in the round caps at 2 even with mission seats (G.3).

dissent.lower: Funding could be 1. Apollo asks the parties it evaluates to pay fair market value, says it ran evaluations for all major labs in 2025, and publishes no revenue split; its 2024 self-report named only about $2M of philanthropy, and its 2026 seed round included Macroscopic Ventures, an Anthropic Series A and B investor. If lab fees are the principal revenue, F.5 caps at 1, and a material lab-investor stake would cap at 1 under F.4.
dissent.higher: Funding could be 3. Apollo's norms bar outcome-contingent pay and side grants or investments from evaluated labs; the PBC post says it remains partly philanthropy-supported, and the index records about $4.4M from Coefficient and $1.1M from SFF. A published cap holding lab revenue at or below 10% of annual revenue, with market rates and publication rights, would lift the F.3 cap to 3, the anchor for mostly philanthropic money with some lab-linked pooled funds.
